Oracle RAC 19c에서 여러 인스턴스가 하나의 DB를 함께 여는: A 10-step animated lesson that dissects how several instances open one database together in Oracle RAC 19c (per-instance SGA, redo thread and undo, shared storage), SCAN and services, Cache Fusion with GCS and GES, gc waits, and how VIPs and services move when a node fails. It also covers a case where a service did not return to its place after the node came back, causing slowness.
After racnode2 rebooted overnight, the morning settlement batch is twice as slow. Dissect RAC, where two servers open one database together, in 10 steps.

서비스가 옮겨 가고 돌아오지 않는 이유: Why services move and do not come back
새벽에 노드가 재부팅된 뒤, 아침 정산 배치가 두 배 느리다: After a node rebooted overnight, the morning batch is twice as slow
결제 DB PAYDB는 racnode1과 racnode2 두 서버를 묶은: The payment database PAYDB is a RAC of two servers, racnode1 and racnode2. The night log says: "03:10 racnode2 rebooted after a hardware alarm, 07:40 confirmed back up." Both nodes are fine now, and PAYDB1 and PAYDB2 are both open.
그런데 아침 정산 배치가 평소보다 두 배 느리고 결제 화면도 조금 느립니: Yet the morning settlement batch is twice as slow as usual and the payment screen is a little slow too. Every server is alive, so what changed? The answer lies in who works where in RAC.
DBA 실습 11단계 졸업 미션(레슨 103)과 같은 장애입니다. 실습에: This is the same incident as the DBA labs stage 11 graduation mission (lesson 103). There you solved it with commands; here you see what happened underneath.
DB는 하나, 인스턴스는 둘: 각자의 SGA, redo thread, U: One database, two instances: each with its own SGA, redo thread and undo
RAC Administration Guide에 따르면 RAC에서는 여러: According to the RAC Administration Guide, in RAC several instances access one database together, each running on a separate server. The data files exist once, on shared storage (here the ASM disk group +DATA).
인스턴스는 각자 SGA와 백그라운드 프로세스를 갖고, 문서대로 각자의 <: Each instance has its own SGA and background processes, and, as the documentation says, its own redo thread and instance-specific undo tablespace. PAYDB1 writes redo to thread 1 and PAYDB2 to thread 2. All of it is on shared storage, so each can read the other's redo.
GV$ 뷰는 열려 있는 모든 인스턴스의 정보를 INST_ID와 함께 보여: GV$ views show information from all open instances along with INST_ID. In DBA lab 101 you compared V$INSTANCE (one row) and GV$INSTANCE (two rows).
+ 데이터 파일: 공유 저장소에 하나: + data files: one set on shared storage
+ 인스턴스마다 SGA · redo thread · Undo: + per instance: SGA · redo thread · undo
SCAN으로 들어와 서비스로 일한다: Come in through SCAN, work through services
앱은 노드 이름이 아니라 <span class=\"term\">SCAN<: The app connects with the SCAN name, not node names. According to the documentation, the SCAN name resolves to three IPs in round robin, and the SCAN listeners send each connection to a suitable instance. The app's connect string stays the same as nodes are added or removed.
앱이 접속할 때 쓰는 것은 <span class=\"term\">서비스<: What the app names when connecting is a service. Each service has preferred instances where it normally runs, and available instances that take over if a preferred one fails. In PAYDB, pay_oltp runs on both instances, and pay_batch runs only on PAYDB2 (preferred), with PAYDB1 available.
결제 화면과 정산 배치를 서비스로 나눠 서로 다른 인스턴스에 두면, 같은: Splitting the payment screen and settlement batch into services on different instances reduces both nodes modifying the same blocks at once. The next scene shows why.
Cache Fusion: 다른 인스턴스 캐시에 있는 블록은 디스크 대신: Cache Fusion: a block in another instance's cache comes over the network, not from disk
PAYDB1이 읽으려는 블록을 PAYDB2가 이미 캐시에 갖고 있으면 어: What if a block PAYDB1 wants is already in PAYDB2's cache? According to the documentation, Cache Fusion sends a copy of the block directly from the holding instance's memory cache to the requesting instance's cache. The caches behave logically as one.
블록은 노드끼리만 쓰는 사설 네트워크, <span class=\"term: Blocks travel over the interconnect, a private network used only between nodes. The documentation explains this is often faster than reading from disk, and that even consistent-read (CR) blocks are obtained from another instance. That is why the interconnect must be a dedicated network of at least Gigabit speed.
빠르다고 공짜는 아닙니다. 두 인스턴스가 같은 블록을 번갈아 고치면 그: Fast is not free. If two instances take turns modifying the same block, it keeps crossing the interconnect, and that means waiting.
누가 어떤 블록을 갖고 있나: GCS, GES, GRD: Who holds which block: GCS, GES and the GRD
블록이 어느 인스턴스에 어떤 모드로 있는지 기억하고 조정하는 것이 <sp: Remembering and coordinating which instance holds a block in which mode is the job of GCS (Global Cache Service); coordinating enqueues such as locks is GES (Global Enqueue Service). According to the documentation, this information lives in the GRD (Global Resource Directory), which is distributed across the active instances.
이 일은 RAC 전용 백그라운드 프로세스가 합니다. 문서대로 <b>LMS: RAC-specific background processes do this work. As the documentation says, LMS transmits block images between buffer caches, LMD handles incoming remote resource requests and deadlock detection, and LMON monitors global resources across the cluster and manages instance deaths and the associated recovery.
리눅스 <code>ps</code>에서 ora_lms0_PAYDB1, o: If Linux ps shows processes like ora_lms0_PAYDB1 and ora_lmon_PAYDB1, it is a RAC instance.
gc로 시작하는 대기: 다른 인스턴스의 블록을 기다린다: Waits starting with gc: waiting for another instance's block
Database Reference의 대기 이벤트 목록에는 gc로 시작하는: The Database Reference wait event list includes global cache waits starting with gc. gc cr request and gc current request mean a block has been requested from another instance and is awaited; gc cr block 2-way means a CR block was received from another instance. gc buffer busy acquire means waiting because another session in the same instance has already requested that block.
이런 대기가 많다는 것은 두 인스턴스가 같은 블록을 자주 주고받는다는 뜻: Many of these waits mean the two instances exchange the same blocks often. They grow especially when sessions on both nodes modify the same blocks of the same table at the same time.
RAC에서 대기를 볼 때는 V$가 아니라 GV$SESSION으로 보고 I: In RAC, look at waits with GV$SESSION, not V$, and split by INST_ID. Looking at one node misses problems on the other.
03:10 racnode2가 죽었을 때: VIP와 복구: 03:10, racnode2 dies: the VIP and recovery
racnode2가 멈추면 PAYDB2도 함께 사라집니다. 문서에 따르면: When racnode2 stops, PAYDB2 disappears with it. According to the documentation, that node's VIP fails over to another node, and clients trying to connect to the relocated VIP get an immediate connection refused error instead of waiting for a TCP timeout, so they can retry another address.
PAYDB2가 쓰다 만 변경은 redo thread 2에 있고, 이 re: PAYDB2's unfinished changes are in redo thread 2, and that redo is on shared storage. As the documentation glossary says, LMON manages instance deaths and the associated recovery, handling the part related to global resources. Meanwhile PAYDB1 stays open.
DBA 실습 레슨 106은 이 일을 계획해서 하는 노드 정비(인스턴스 비: DBA lab 106 is the planned version: node maintenance (draining the instance and restarting Clusterware). The difference between a failure and maintenance is whether sessions were moved first.
pay_batch는 available로 옮겨 가고, 저절로 돌아오지 않는: pay_batch moves to its available instance and does not come back on its own
preferred 인스턴스(PAYDB2)가 사라지자 Clusterware: When the preferred instance (PAYDB2) disappeared, Clusterware moved pay_batch to its available instance, PAYDB1. The settlement batch can keep running on PAYDB1.
07:40에 racnode2와 PAYDB2가 돌아왔습니다. 하지만 RAC: At 07:40 racnode2 and PAYDB2 came back. But according to the RAC Administration Guide, Oracle does not automatically move the service back to the preferred instance when it restarts. From 19.3, giving the service the -failback option makes it return when a preferred instance becomes available.
노드 복구 뒤 점검 목록에 \"서비스가 제자리에 있나(srvctl sta: Always add "are services where they belong (srvctl status service)" to the post-recovery checklist. DBA lab 102 practices the command for moving services.
사례 해결: 한 노드에 몰린 일을 서비스로 다시 나눈다: Fix: split the work piled on one node back out by service
1장면의 원인입니다. PAYDB1에 결제 세션과 정산 배치가 함께 몰려: This is the cause from scene 1. Payment sessions and the settlement batch piled onto PAYDB1, competing for CPU, and exchanging the same blocks with PAYDB2's payment sessions raised gc waits. Every server is alive, but the work is lopsided.
정산팀과 시점을 정한 뒤 <code>srvctl relocate serv: After agreeing on timing with the settlement team, move pay_batch back to PAYDB2 with srvctl relocate service. Without -force, running batch sessions are not killed; new work goes to PAYDB2. To prevent recurrence, add a service location check after node recovery to the runbook, or consider -failback.
RAC 장애는 \"서버가 죽었다\"보다 \"죽었다 살아난 뒤 상태가 평소: RAC failures show up more often as "things differ from normal after it came back" than as "a server died". Always check service locations and which instance sessions have piled onto.
정리: 데이터는 하나, 일은 서비스로 나눈다: Recap: one set of data, work divided by services
RAC는 공유 저장소의 DB 하나를 여러 인스턴스가 함께 엽니다. 인스턴: RAC has several instances open one database on shared storage. Each instance has its own SGA, redo thread and undo, and blocks in another instance's cache arrive over the interconnect by Cache Fusion. GCS and GES coordinate this with the GRD, and LMS, LMD and LMON do the work.
앱은 SCAN과 서비스로 접속하고, 노드가 죽으면 VIP와 서비스가 옮겨: Apps connect through SCAN and services, and when a node dies its VIP and services move. Services do not come back on their own, though, so after a node returns, check where services run and move them back.
